what-is-maestro-pro: What Maestro Pro is. Maestro Pro is an app for musicians that reads your scores, follows them to the note and plays along. Maestro Pro is a working tool for musicians. It reads your scores and follows them to the note, turns pages for you, and rehearses with a backing track, a song from Apple Music, the built-in instrument or a metronome. It also lets you write and revise the music itself. It runs on iPhone, iPad and Mac. You can slow a hard passage down without changing the pitch, transpose for your instrument, record yourself against the score, and play along with other devices.
your-first-minute: Your first minute. Import a score, press Play and tap the music to start from any point. 1. Tap Import Score on the home screen (or the + button, then Import Score) and choose a PDF, MusicXML file or any other supported file. 2. The score appears in your library on the left. Tap it to open it. 3. Press the big Play button at the bottom. The music plays and follows along. Tap anywhere on the music to start from there, or drag the progress bar.
open-the-sample-score: Open the sample score. Try the app straight away with the built-in sample, no files needed. Nothing to play yet? Choose Open Sample on the home screen and the app opens a sample score for you to try. You can also use Search Scores to download classical pieces and jazz tunes, or to search the web. Searching needs an internet connection.
find-free-scores: Find free scores with Search Scores. Search Scores downloads classical pieces and jazz tunes, and searches the web for free scores. Choose Search Scores on the home screen to download classical pieces and jazz tunes, or to search the web for free scores. Downloading a free score fetches it from the site that hosts it. Search Scores needs the internet, and it is part of the Performer and Professional plans. The Free plan does not include anything that needs the internet.
free-plan-limits: What the Free plan includes. The Free plan keeps up to three scores and lets you view and play them, with some tools left for paid plans. On the Free plan you can keep up to three scores and view the sheet music for each. You can open lyrics files, play along with your own audio files, connect your own GitHub repositories and add tracks from them, and make scales and arpeggios in any key. The built-in synth instruments play the score, but nothing follows along on the page: there is no note highlighting, bar highlighting or moving line until Performer. Nothing that needs the internet is included, and there is no equaliser, key changes or other tools.
plans-and-pricing: Plans and pricing. Free, Performer and Professional: what each plan includes, and how to buy. Maestro Pro has three plans: Free, Performer and Professional. The paid plans are subscriptions, managed in your Apple Account settings, and their prices are shown in the app in your own currency. Buying on this website is for Professional only, not Performer. It is £10 per month on a 12-month contract or £89 per year, or the equivalent in your local currency. That is cheaper than buying the Performer plan in the app, and it includes the score editor.
free-plan: The Free plan. What you get for nothing: up to three scores, viewing, lyrics files, your own audio, GitHub and scales. The Free plan keeps up to three scores and lets you view the sheet music for each. You can open lyrics files, play along with your own audio files, connect your own GitHub repositories and add tracks from them, and make scales and arpeggios in any key. It does not include note, bar or moving-line highlighting, anything that needs the internet, an equaliser, key changes or other tools. The free version can be rolled out to a whole school through Apple's volume purchasing.
performer-plan: The Performer plan. Everything except the score editor, with a library of any size. Performer includes everything except the score editor. You get a library of any size, and notes, bars and a moving line that follow the music. It also includes Search Scores and lyrics online, key changes and the equaliser, backing tracks and Apple Music, Play Together, the tuner, Wait for Me, recording and review, annotation, and export and print. Performer is a subscription you start inside the app, managed in your Apple Account settings. It is not sold on this website.
professional-plan: The Professional plan. Everything, including the score editor, medleys and version history with GitHub sync. Professional includes everything, including the score editor. You can write and change music, build medleys, and keep version history with branches, merges and GitHub sync. You can buy Professional on this website for £10 per month on a 12-month contract or £89 per year. A licence bought on the website works on up to 3 devices. It can also be bought in the app as a subscription.
compare-plans: Which plan do I need?. A quick way to choose between Free, Performer and Professional. - Free is for reading your part: up to three scores, viewing, lyrics files, your own audio, GitHub and scales. - Performer is for practising with the full set of tools, except the editor: highlighting that follows the music, search, backing tracks and Apple Music, Play Together, the tuner, Wait for Me, recording and review, annotation, export and print. - Professional is for anyone who writes or arranges music: everything in Performer, plus the score editor, medleys and version history with GitHub sync. Teachers and schools can also read Education and schools.
buy-on-the-website: Buy Professional on this website. Pay monthly or yearly on the website, then recover your licence key and install the app. Go to the buy page, enter your name and email, choose £89 per year or £10 per month (a 12-month contract), and continue to the secure payment page. After you pay, recover your licence key using the email address you paid with. We email you the key and the TestFlight install link. In the app, tap "Already have a licence key?" on the paywall and enter it. A licence bought on the website works on up to 3 devices. You can remove a device at any time to free its place. If you already have an active licence for your email address, the buy page tells you and links to key recovery instead of letting you pay twice.
website-or-in-app: Website or in-app: which is cheaper?. Professional bought on the website costs less than Performer bought in the app, and includes the editor. Buying Professional on this website is cheaper than buying the Performer plan in the app, and it includes the score editor. Performer is not sold on the website. Plans bought inside the app are subscriptions managed in your Apple Account settings, and refunds for them are requested from Apple. A licence bought on the website is managed with us: your key arrives by email and cancellation is requested on the cancellation page.
prices-and-currency: Prices and currencies. Website prices are in pounds sterling or the local equivalent, and app prices show in your own currency. Prices on the website are in pounds sterling, or the equivalent in your local currency. Prices for plans bought in the app are shown in the app, in your own currency.
manage-an-apple-subscription: Manage a subscription bought in the app. Performer and Professional bought in the app are managed in your Apple Account settings. The paid plans bought inside the app are subscriptions, managed in your Apple Account settings. (If your plan comes from a licence key instead, Settings shows Manage Licence: see Manage your licence in the app.) That is where you change or stop them. To ask for a refund on a subscription bought in the app, see Refunds for subscriptions bought in the app. Licences bought on the website are different: see Refunds and cancellation.
licences-and-keys: Licences and keys. How your licence key works, how to enter it and what to do if you lose it. A licence bought on the website comes with a licence key. You enter the key in the app to unlock it. Maestro Pro needs a licence to be used. A licence works on up to 3 devices. The key is emailed to the address you paid with, together with the TestFlight link to install the app. If you lose it, you can have it sent again from the key page.
enter-your-licence-key: Enter your licence key in the app. On the paywall, tap Already have a licence key? and type your key. 1. Open Maestro Pro. 2. On the paywall, tap Already have a licence key? 3. Enter your licence key. The key works on up to 3 devices. If you are told the limit has been reached, remove a device you no longer use and enter the key again. If you do not have your key to hand, recover your licence key first.
recover-your-licence-key: Recover a lost licence key. Enter the email address you paid with and the key is emailed to you. Open the key page, enter the email address you paid with, and press Email me my key. If we find your payment, we email you your licence key along with the TestFlight link to install the app. The key is only ever sent to your inbox, never shown on the page. Use the email address you paid with. If nothing arrives, check your spam folder.
manage-your-licence-in-the-app: Manage your licence in the app. With a licence key, Settings shows Manage Licence: remove a device or request a cancellation. When your plan comes from a licence key, Settings shows Manage Licence in place of Manage Subscription (which is for plans bought with the App Store). Tap Manage Licence and choose: - Remove A Device opens the devices page, where you enter your key to see the devices using it and remove one. See Remove a device from your licence. - Request Cancellation opens the cancellation page, which checks your key and shows what will happen before anything is cancelled or charged. See How to request a refund or cancel. Both pages open inside the app.
devices-per-licence: Use your licence on up to 3 devices. A licence bought on the website works on up to 3 devices. Education licences have no limit. A licence bought on the website works on up to 3 devices: for example an iPhone, an iPad and a Mac. Enter the same key on each one. A device is counted the first time it is used with the key, and the key is checked each time the app is opened. If you try a fourth device, Maestro Pro says the licence is already in use on 3 devices. Remove a device you no longer use to free its place, then enter your key again. A device that has not been used for 60 days stops counting automatically. If you delete the app and install it again, that counts as a new device until the old one is removed or ages out, so remove the old one if you reach the limit. Education licences, bought for a whole organisation, have no device limit. See Buy for a whole organisation.
remove-a-device: Remove a device from your licence. Use the devices page on the key page to see where your licence is used and remove a device. 1. Open the devices page. 2. Enter your licence key and choose Show my devices. 3. Find the device you no longer use. If you are not sure which it is, open Maestro Pro on it and choose Refresh: the device you just used moves to the top with a new last used time. 4. Choose Remove next to the device you want to take off. The place is free straight away, so you can enter your key on another device. A removed device is signed out the next time Maestro Pro checks the licence, which is each time the app is opened. You can use Remove all devices to start again. If you do not have your key, recover your licence key first.
several-licence-keys: If you have more than one licence key. If you have subscribed more than once, the email lists every active key with its plan. If you have subscribed more than once with the same email address, the key email lists every active key and names the plan each one belongs to. Use the key for the plan you want to use. Cancelled keys are not included.
licence-key-not-working: My licence key is not working. Check the key, check it is still active, and recover it again if needed. - Check the key was typed exactly as sent. Copying it from the email is the safest way. - If the key was cancelled, it stops working after the date given in the cancellation email. - If you have more than one key, try the one for your current plan. See more than one licence key. - If it says the licence is already in use on 3 devices, remove a device and try again. - Recover your licence key to get a fresh email with every active key.
install-and-testflight: Install with TestFlight. Maestro Pro is installed through Apple's TestFlight app until it reaches the App Store. Maestro Pro is installed through Apple's TestFlight app until it reaches the App Store, which is coming soon. You need a licence to use it.
install-with-testflight: Install Maestro Pro step by step. Install TestFlight, accept the invitation, install Maestro Pro, then enter your key. 1. Install TestFlight from the App Store on your iPhone, iPad or Mac. 2. Open the Maestro Pro invitation and tap Accept, then Install. 3. Open Maestro Pro. Tap "Already have a licence key?" on the paywall and enter your key. The install link comes in the email that carries your licence key.
lost-the-testflight-link: I lost the TestFlight link. The key email includes the TestFlight link, and the install page has it too. The email that carries your licence key also includes the TestFlight install link, so recovering your licence key sends it again. The install page shows the link as well.
refunds-and-cancellation: Refunds and cancellation. The 14-day money-back guarantee, and how to cancel a licence bought on the website. Licences bought on the website have a 14-day money-back guarantee. Refunds and cancellations cannot be done by email: they are requested on the cancellation page, which checks your licence key and shows exactly what will happen before anything is cancelled or charged. Subscribed inside the app through the App Store? Apple handles those payments, so ask Apple for the refund: Request a refund for apps or content you bought from Apple. See Refunds for subscriptions bought in the app.
money-back-guarantee: The 14-day money-back guarantee. Ask for a full refund within 14 days of your first payment, once the payment has cleared. If Maestro Pro is not for you, you can ask for a full refund within 14 days of your first payment. Bank payments take about a week to clear, and a payment can only be refunded once it has. So you can ask from the 8th day on and by the 14th day. When the refund is made, your licence, subscription and any future payments are cancelled.
how-to-request-a-refund: How to request a refund or cancel. Use the cancellation page with your licence key and follow the steps. This is for licences bought on this website. If you subscribed inside the app through the App Store, ask Apple instead: request a refund from Apple. 1. Have your licence key ready. If you have lost it, recover your licence key first. 2. Open the cancellation page and enter your key. 3. Check what the page says will happen. Nothing is cancelled or charged until you confirm. 4. You may be asked why you are cancelling, then confirm. You receive a confirmation email saying the licence has been cancelled, any refund or fee, and the last day you can use the licence.
refund-for-app-store-subscriptions: Refunds for subscriptions bought in the app. If you subscribed inside the app through the App Store, Apple handles the refund, not us. If you subscribed inside the app, Apple took the payment and Apple decides refunds, so we cannot refund it and our cancellation page will not find it. Ask Apple directly: request a refund for apps or content you bought from Apple. Apple's page walks you through it. In short, you sign in with the Apple Account that bought the subscription, choose the purchase and say why you want a refund. Apple replies by email with its decision. To stop the subscription renewing, cancel it in your Apple Account settings. See manage a subscription bought in the app. Not sure where you bought it? A licence key that arrived by email means you bought on this website, so use the cancellation page. No key, and you subscribed on the paywall inside the app, means Apple.
refund-timing: When can I get a refund?. Refunds are made from day 8 to day 14 after the first payment, once it has cleared. - Days 0 to 7: the payment has not cleared yet, so it cannot be refunded. The cancellation page tells you the date to come back, the 8th day after your payment. - Days 8 to 14: you can be refunded in full. - Day 15 onwards: the guarantee has ended. See after the 14 days.
after-the-14-days: Cancelling after the 14 days. No refund, but you can cancel going forward, and how that works differs for yearly and monthly plans. After the 14 days we cannot refund your payments, but you can cancel so that nothing more is taken. What happens depends on how you pay: - Yearly licence: the subscription is cancelled and your key keeps working to the end of the year you paid for. - Monthly licence: a cancellation fee is taken, then your remaining payments stop.
cancel-a-yearly-licence: Cancel a yearly licence. Your yearly subscription is cancelled and the key works until the end of the year you paid for. After the 14 days, cancelling a yearly licence stops it renewing. Your licence key keeps working until the end of the year you paid for, and the cancellation email gives that date.
cancel-a-monthly-licence: Cancel a monthly licence. Monthly licences are on a 12-month contract, so cancelling early costs one month plus half of the remaining term. Monthly licences are on a 12-month contract. After the 14 days, ending it early costs one month plus half of the remaining term. The cancellation page shows the exact amount before you confirm, and collects it from the bank account you already paid from. Your remaining monthly payments are then cancelled and your key keeps working until the date in the confirmation email.
education-and-schools: Education and schools. How schools, colleges and tutors can get Maestro Pro, including volume licensing outside the App Store. Maestro Pro is for music schools, music services, colleges and private tutors as well as individuals. The education page describes how it helps students practise and tutors teach. There are two ways to buy for a group: Apple's volume purchasing for the free version, and a single licence for a whole organisation bought direct from us.
apple-volume-purchasing: Apple volume purchasing. Schools can roll the free version out through Apple School Manager or Apple Business Manager. Apple lets schools and organisations buy apps in bulk through Apps and Books in Apple School Manager or Apple Business Manager, both free to enrol and needing the organisation to be verified by Apple. The free version of Maestro Pro can be rolled out to every device this way. Performer and Professional are subscriptions, and Apple's volume purchasing covers apps rather than subscriptions, so each person who needs a paid plan subscribes on their own Apple Account. Volume purchasing is not offered in every country or region.
buy-for-your-organisation: Buy for a whole organisation. One licence for unlimited students and teachers, £499 a year, bought direct and outside the App Store. You can buy one licence that covers a whole school, college, music service or tuition business, straight from us and outside the App Store. It is £499 a year for unlimited students and teachers, with every Maestro Pro feature, including the score editor, medleys and version history with GitHub sync. There is no per-seat counting and no Apple School Manager or Apple Business Manager set-up. An organisation licence has no device limit, unlike a single licence, which works on up to 3 devices (see Use your licence on up to 3 devices). You pay through our secure payment page, then recover your licence key with the email address you paid with. The details are on the education page.
student-licence: The student licence. Students can buy Professional for £48 a year or £6 a month on a 12-month contract. The students page sells Professional to students at £48 per year, or £6 per month on a 12-month contract. A student licence works on up to 3 devices. After you pay, use the students key page to have your licence key emailed to you.
supported-file-types: Supported file types. PDF, MusicXML, MIDI, karaoke, lyrics, CD+Graphics and Maestro Pro files can all be imported. Import Score takes: - PDF - MusicXML (.musicxml, .xml, .mxl) - MIDI and karaoke (.mid, .kar) - lyrics (.lrc, .txt) - CD+Graphics karaoke (.cdg) - Maestro Pro (.maestropro) files Band-in-a-Box files cannot be read, because that is a closed format. See Band-in-a-Box files.
import-a-score: Import a score. Tap Import Score, choose your files, and they appear in the library. Tap Import Score on the home screen (or the + button, then Import Score) and choose a file. It appears in your library. Tap it to open it. You can choose several files at once. Other ways in are dragging files onto the window, the share sheet of another app, and importing a whole folder.
import-a-pdf: Import a PDF score. PDFs are read by the app, which only reads printed notation, and scans need to be straight and clear. Import a PDF with Import Score like any other file. The app reads the notation from the page and then follows it as it plays. Only printed notation can be read, and a scan needs to be straight and clear. If the app reads a scan badly, import a MusicXML file of the piece instead; many are free online. If a PDF plays the wrong number of beats, see a PDF plays the wrong number of beats.
import-musicxml-files: Import MusicXML files. MusicXML files (.musicxml, .xml, .mxl) import like any other score and can be edited. Import MusicXML (.musicxml, .xml or .mxl) with Import Score. It is the best format for a score you want to edit, because the score editor changes the notes in a MusicXML score. If a scan reads badly, a MusicXML file of the piece is the reliable alternative.
import-midi-and-karaoke-files: Import MIDI and karaoke files. MIDI and karaoke (.mid, .kar) files import with Import Score; karaoke files carry their own words. Import MIDI and karaoke files (.mid, .kar) with Import Score. Karaoke MIDI (.kar) files contain their own words, so lyrics appear without a separate file. See karaoke MIDI files.
import-several-files: Import several files at once. Choose more than one file in the import dialog and they all arrive together. Import Score lets you choose several files at once. To bring in everything in a folder, use Import Folder.
drag-files-onto-the-window: Drag files onto the window. Drag files from the Files app straight onto the Maestro Pro window to import them. Drag files from the Files app straight onto the Maestro Pro window to import them. If a file is greyed out or Import Score does nothing, see Import does nothing or shows a file greyed out.
import-from-another-app: Import from another app's share sheet. Choose Maestro Pro in the share sheet of Files, Mail, Safari, Messages and other apps. Choose Maestro Pro from the share sheet of another app (Files, Mail, Safari, Messages and others) to import what you are looking at. This works for a score attached to an email or found on a website.
import-a-folder: Import a whole folder. Import Folder reads every supported file in a folder. Import Folder reads every supported file in a folder. If you want new files to keep appearing by themselves, link a folder instead.
link-a-folder: Link a folder to the library. In Settings, Link a Folder keeps a folder in step with the library so new files appear by themselves. In Settings, Link a Folder keeps a folder in step with the library, so new files appear in the library by themselves.
start-a-blank-score: Start a blank score. New Blank Score creates an empty score with the name, time signature, key, bars, staves and tempo you choose. New Blank Score starts an empty score to write yourself. You choose the name, time signature, key, number of bars, staves (treble, bass or piano) and tempo. Writing and editing needs the score editor, which is part of the Professional plan.
add-lyrics-with-backing: Lyrics with Backing. Choose a backing track and the app finds its timed lyrics online for a karaoke-style screen. Lyrics with Backing: choose a backing track and the app finds its timed lyrics online, for a karaoke-style screen. You can also choose a lyrics file along with the backing track. Finding lyrics online needs the internet.
icloud-library: Keep your library in iCloud. Your library is stored on the device and is also kept in iCloud when iCloud Drive is on. Everything you import lives in the library and stays on the device. If you turn on iCloud Drive, it is also kept in the app's iCloud folder in your own iCloud account, so it is available on your other devices. That storage belongs to you and Apple; the developer cannot see it.
set-lists: Set-lists for rehearsals and gigs. Build set-lists for a lesson, a rehearsal or a concert. Maestro Pro supports set-lists for a lesson, a rehearsal or a concert, so the pieces you need are together in the library.
import-band-in-a-box-files: Band-in-a-Box files. Band-in-a-Box files cannot be read; export MusicXML and audio from Band-in-a-Box instead. Band-in-a-Box files cannot be read, because that is a closed format. In Band-in-a-Box, save as MusicXML for the notation and as audio for the backing, then import both.
play-and-pause: Play, pause and skip. The bar at the bottom has Play and Pause, skip by bar and a progress bar you can drag. The bar at the bottom controls playback: Play and Pause, skip back and forward by bar, and a progress bar you can drag. The counter shows the bar, beat and time.
jump-to-a-bar: Start from any bar. Tap the music to jump to that point, or drag the progress bar. Tap anywhere on the music to start from there. You can also drag the progress bar, or skip back and forward by bar.
mac-playback-keys: Playback keys on a Mac. Space plays and pauses, arrows skip bars, Return goes to the start and K toggles the metronome. On a Mac, Space plays and pauses, the arrow keys skip bars, Return goes to the start and K turns the metronome on or off. On a Mac or with a keyboard, [ slows the practice speed and ] speeds it up. You can change any shortcut: see Keyboard shortcuts.
change-practice-speed: Slow down or speed up without changing pitch. Practice Speed runs from 10 to 400 percent and keeps the pitch the same. Practice Speed slows a piece down or speeds it up without changing the pitch. Type any percentage from 10 to 400 in the box, or use the slider (50 to 150). On a Mac or with a keyboard, [ slows it and ] speeds it up.
tempo-and-custom-tempo: Tempo and Custom Tempo. The tempo is the score's own unless you set one; Custom Tempo goes back to the score's. The tempo is the score's own, from its printed metronome mark, unless you set one. Typing a BPM, tapping it or matching a backing track makes it your own, and the Custom Tempo switch under the tempo goes back to the score's.
tap-the-tempo: Tap the tempo. Tap the tempo, then tap the Tap key in time with the beat and the tempo follows you. Tap the tempo (the note and number beside the metronome) and a pad opens with a big Tap key. Tap it in time with the beat. The tempo appears from the second tap and updates with every tap, and a few more make it steadier. It is set as you tap. With a keyboard, the space bar taps while the key is focused. The same pad is under Tempo in the Inspector.
loop-a-passage: Loop a hard passage. In the Inspector, Loop plays the bars you choose over and over. In the Inspector, Loop plays the bars you choose over and over, to practise a hard passage. Pair it with a slower practice speed and speed it up again when the passage is ready.
count-in-and-lead-in-bars: Count In and Lead-in Bars. Count In plays a bar of clicks first; Lead-in Bars sets how many bars of introduction come before bar 1. Count In plays a bar of clicks before the music. Lead-in Bars sets how many bars of introduction come before bar 1, so a backing track with an intro lines up.
use-the-metronome: Use the metronome. The metronome clicks on every beat and can be turned on and off, with K on a Mac. The Metronome clicks on every beat. On a Mac, K turns it on or off. While you record, the metronome is muted so the microphone hears only you.
transpose-for-your-instrument: Transpose for your instrument. Transposing typesets the score again in the new key, rather than just labelling it. Transpose for your clarinet, trumpet or saxophone, and the score is typeset again in the new key rather than just labelled. Key changes are part of the Performer and Professional plans.
set-your-instrument: Set your instrument. Setting your instrument to B flat or E flat in the Inspector shows the written note in the tuner. Set your instrument in the Inspector. If it is set to B♭ or E♭, the tuner shows the written note too. See Tune a B♭ or E♭ instrument.
page-turning: Automatic page turning. The page scrolls or curls over like a real book exactly when you need it. When you press Play, the music follows itself. The page scrolls or curls over like a real book exactly when you need it, so you do not need to turn pages by hand.
note-and-bar-highlighting: Notes and bars that light up. Notes glow as they sound and a soft wash marks the bar; this needs the Performer plan or above. Notes glow as they sound, a soft wash marks the bar, and a moving line follows the music. This is part of the Performer and Professional plans: on the Free plan nothing follows along on the page. Choose the colour in Highlight Colour.
use-the-inspector: The Inspector. The Inspector holds tempo, practice speed, loop, key, instrument and backing tracks. The toolbar and the Inspector change how a score looks and sounds. The Inspector is where you find tempo, practice speed, loop, key, instrument and backing tracks, and where you can add another backing track.
open-the-tuner: Open the tuner. The Tuner is on the home screen, the + menu, Settings under Listening, and the tuning fork in a score's toolbar. Open the Tuner from the home screen, the + menu, Settings ▸ Listening, or the tuning fork in a score's toolbar. The tuner listens through the microphone, so allow microphone access when asked. Sound is analysed on the device and is never recorded or sent anywhere. The tuner is part of the Performer and Professional plans.
read-the-tuner-display: Read the tuner display. It shows the note name, how many cents sharp or flat you are, and the frequency, with a needle and an eight-second trace. Play a note and the display shows its name, how many cents sharp or flat it is (a cent is a hundredth of a semitone), and the frequency. The needle sits in the green zone when you are in tune, and the trace below shows the last eight seconds.
play-a-reference-note: Play a reference note. Play Reference Note sounds the note you are aiming for. Play Reference Note sounds the note you are aiming for, so you can tune by ear as well as by the needle.
change-concert-pitch: Change the tuning pitch (A = 440 Hz). A = 440 Hz can be changed between 415 and 466 for baroque or orchestral tuning. A = 440 Hz can be changed to any value from 415 to 466 Hz, for baroque or orchestral tuning.
tune-a-b-flat-or-e-flat-instrument: Tune a B flat or E flat instrument. With your instrument set to B flat or E flat in the Inspector, the tuner shows the written note too. If your instrument is set to B♭ or E♭ in the Inspector, the tuner shows the written note too, as well as the sounding note. Set the instrument first: see Set your instrument.
what-is-wait-for-me: What is Wait for Me?. Wait for Me holds the score until the right note is played in tune. Wait for Me holds the score until you play the right note in tune, so you can work through a piece note by note at your own pace. It listens through the microphone, and the sound is analysed on the device. Wait for Me is part of the Performer and Professional plans. If it says it cannot hear you, see The microphone cannot hear me.
steady-note-trainer: The steady-note trainer. A trainer that listens as you hold a note steady, alongside the tuner and Wait for Me. The tuner and Wait for Me are joined by a steady-note trainer, which uses the microphone to help you hold a note steady. It is part of the listening tools in the Performer and Professional plans.
record-yourself: Record yourself. Press Record, play along after the count-in, then press Stop. Choose Record: the round record button in the toolbar, More ▸ Record Myself, or ⌘R on a Mac. After the count-in the score plays and you play along. Press Stop, or pause, when you have finished. While you record, the built-in instrument and the metronome are muted, so the microphone hears only you. The first time, the app asks to use the microphone.
record-with-a-backing-track: Record when the score has a backing track. The app asks first, because the microphone would hear the backing: Mute It and Record, or Record Anyway. If the score has a backing track, the app asks before recording, because the microphone would hear it. Choose Mute It and Record (the track comes back afterwards), or Record Anyway if you use headphones. The recording bar has a Mute It button too.
review-your-recording: Review your take. The take is shown with the notes lit: green where you should have been, red where you actually were. After recording, review the take with the notes lit: green where you should have been, red where you actually were. It listens through the microphone, so it works with any instrument or your voice, and it shows wrong notes, late entries and the bars to work on.
where-recordings-are-kept: Where recordings are kept. Recordings are kept with the score, copied when you duplicate it, and compressed to well under a megabyte a minute. Recordings are kept with the score, so they are copied when you duplicate it. Each one is compressed to well under a megabyte a minute. Recordings are saved only in your library on your device, and are never sent to us.
make-a-scale: Make a scale or arpeggio. Choose Scales & Arpeggios on the home screen, pick the kind and a key, and a score is created for you. Choose Scales & Arpeggios on the home screen, pick the kind and a key. A score is created for it and added to the library, ready to play, transpose and slow down.
scale-types-and-keys: Scale types and keys. Major, minor, blues, arpeggios and more, in any key. You can pick the kind of scale (major, minor, blues, arpeggios and more) and a key, and make them in any key. Material is made on demand.
scales-are-free: Scales are free on every plan. Making scales and arpeggios in any key is included on the Free plan too. Scales and arpeggios in any key are free on every plan, including the Free plan.
draw-on-a-score: Draw on a score. Turn on Annotate in the toolbar and draw; the ink is saved with the score and shows while you play. Turn on Annotate in the toolbar and draw with Apple Pencil using the tool palette. Ink is saved with the score and shows while you play. Annotation is part of the Performer and Professional plans.
annotation-tools: Annotation tools. Pens, markers, pencil, colours and an eraser. The tool palette has pens, markers, a pencil, colours and an eraser, so you can mark a score up like a paper part.
annotation-zoom-sizes: Annotations and zoom. Each zoom size keeps its own drawing so it stays lined up with the music. Each zoom size keeps its own drawing, so your ink stays lined up with the music. A drawing made at one zoom size does not appear at another.
annotate-on-a-mac: Annotate on a Mac. On a Mac you draw with the trackpad or mouse instead of Apple Pencil. Annotating on iPad uses Apple Pencil, so your finger still scrolls and taps. On a Mac you draw with the trackpad or mouse.
export-with-your-ink: Export and print with your ink. Export as PDF and Print include your ink for the key and zoom you are viewing. Export as PDF and Print include your ink for the key and zoom you are viewing.
add-a-backing-track: Add a backing track. Add the first backing track with Add Backing Track, and it plays in time with the score. A backing track is a recording that plays with the score. Add the first with Add Backing Track. You can play along with your own audio files even on the Free plan; backing tracks and Apple Music with all their tools are part of Performer and Professional.
add-another-backing-track: Add more than one backing track. A score can have several tracks, for example a rhythm section and a separate guide vocal. A score can have more than one backing track, for example a rhythm section and a separate guide vocal. Use Add Another Backing Track in the Inspector or the sound menu. They all play together, in time with the score.
backing-track-levels-and-switches: Track switches and levels. Each track has its own switch and its own level from minus 24 to plus 12 decibels. Under Backing Tracks & Sound each track has its own switch, to turn it off without removing it, and its own level from -24 to +12 decibels.
the-first-backing-track: The first track keeps time. The first backing track is the one the score keeps time with; later tracks follow its speed and key. The first track is the one the score keeps time with, and Match Key & Tempo and the track editor work on it. The other tracks follow its speed and key, but not its edit lanes, and should be recordings that start together with it.
match-key-and-tempo: Match Key and Tempo to a track. Match Key & Tempo works on the first backing track; use it again if the track starts late or early. Match Key & Tempo sets the score to the key and tempo of the first backing track. Typing a tempo or tapping it makes the tempo your own, and matching a backing track does too. If a track starts late or early, see A backing track starts late or early.
reduce-vocals: Reduce vocals on a track. Reduce Vocals cuts the singer down in a stereo recording; it cannot remove a voice from a mono recording. Reduce Vocals, on any track, cuts the singer down in a stereo recording by cancelling what is in the middle. It leaves a mono track, can take some middle instruments with it, and cannot remove a voice from a mono recording.
play-along-with-apple-music: Play along with Apple Music. Play a song from your Apple Music subscription alongside a score and see its lyrics. With an Apple Music subscription you can play a song alongside a score and see its lyrics. It uses Apple's own service under your account. Apple Music is part of the Performer and Professional plans.
built-in-instrument: The built-in instrument. The built-in instrument can play the notes on the page, as can a metronome. The built-in instrument can play the notes on the page too. You can rehearse against it, a backing track, a song from Apple Music, or just a metronome. On the Free plan the synth instruments play the score but nothing follows along on the page.
equaliser-and-key-changes: Equaliser and key changes. Key changes and the equaliser are part of the Performer and Professional plans. Key changes and the equaliser are included in Performer and Professional. They are not part of the Free plan.
add-a-lyrics-file: Add a lyrics file. Add a .lrc file (timed lines) or a .txt file to a score from the Lyrics menu. Add a .lrc file (timed lines) or a .txt file to a score from the Lyrics menu. You can open lyrics files on the Free plan too.
show-lyrics-instead-of-music: Show lyrics instead of music. Show Lyrics Instead of Music swaps the page for the words, which scroll in time like Apple Music. Show Lyrics Instead of Music swaps the page for the words. Lyrics scroll in time with the music like in Apple Music.
animate-syllables: Animate syllables. Animate Syllables swells each syllable as it is sung, and Show Syllable Progress fills it. Animate Syllables swells each syllable as it is sung, and Show Syllable Progress fills it.
lyrics-appearance-settings: Lyrics typeface, size and blur. Typeface, size, alignment and blur for lines not being sung are set in Settings. Typeface, size, alignment and the blur for lines not being sung are in Settings.
lyrics-only-items: Lyrics-only items. A lyrics-only item has its own screen with a transport bar and an optional backing track. A lyrics-only item (no notation) has its own screen with a transport bar and an optional backing track.
lyrics-timing: Lyrics in seconds or in bars. When a lyrics file has no timing, you can choose whether lyrics are timed in seconds or in bars. Lyrics in seconds or in bars can be chosen when the file has no timing, such as a plain .txt file.
karaoke-midi-files: Karaoke MIDI (.kar) files. Karaoke MIDI files contain their own words. Karaoke MIDI (.kar) files contain their own words, so you do not need a separate lyrics file. Import them with Import Score.
cdg-karaoke: CD+Graphics karaoke (.cdg). CD+Graphics karaoke files show their built-in pictures. CD+Graphics karaoke files (.cdg) show their built-in pictures. Import them with Import Score.
find-lyrics-online: Find lyrics and singers online. Lyrics and singers can be found online; this needs the internet and sends the song title and artist to lyric services. The app can find lyrics and singers online when you ask it to. Searching sends your search words (and, to match singers, the song title and artist) to LRCLIB (lyrics) and Genius (singers). Nothing is sent unless you ask. See When the app uses the internet.
duets-and-singers: Duets and singers. Duets get a singer each, in their own colour. For duets, lyrics give each singer their own colour, so you can see whose line is whose.
open-the-score-editor: Open the score editor. Edit Score opens the editor, which works on MusicXML scores and on a copy of what the app read from a PDF. The score editor changes the notes in a MusicXML score. Open it with Edit Score, the music-note-list button. In Simple mode the button appears for scores you created. The editor is part of the Professional plan.
the-nine-editor-modes: The nine editor modes. One strip of nine modes at the bottom of the editor: Notes, Rests, Marks, Dynamics, Bars, Form, Medley, Erase and Draw. The strip at the bottom of the editor has one mode for each kind of job, so the controls for a job are together. Swipe the strip for the rest. The modes are: - Notes - Rests - Marks - Dynamics - Bars - Form - Medley - Erase - Draw
editor-notes-mode: Notes mode: add and move notes. Slide on a rest to choose a pitch, lift to place a note, drag to move one, scribble to rub it out. Touch a rest and slide up or down to choose the pitch; lift to put a note there, as long as the length chosen below. Drag a note up or down to move it. Scribble back and forth over a note to rub it out. Select a note, then tap a length to change how long it lasts.
editor-rests-mode: Rests mode. Turn a note into a rest, change a rest's length, or take a rest off the page. Tap a note to turn it into a rest of the chosen length. Tap a rest to select it and change its length, or use the bin to take it off the page (the bar keeps its length).
editor-marks-mode: Marks mode: accidentals, ties and articulations. Add a sharp, flat or natural, tie notes, or give a note staccato, accent, tenuto, marcato or a fermata. Tap a note, then add a sharp, flat or natural, tie it to the next note, or give it staccato, accent, tenuto, marcato or a fermata. Tap one again to take it off.
editor-dynamics-mode: Dynamics mode. Put dynamics from ppp to fff on a note or bar, and crescendo or diminuendo hairpins over bars. Tap a note (the dynamic goes at that note) or a bar (at its start), then choose ppp to fff. Crescendo and Diminuendo put a hairpin over the bar; Longer and Shorter stretch it over more bars.
editor-bars-mode: Bars mode: repeats, adding and deleting bars. Repeat signs, adding a bar before or after, deleting one or several bars, and Expand Repeats to write a piece out as it is played. Tap a bar to choose it. Start and End put repeat signs on it (End cycles through two, three and four times). Add Bar Before and Add Bar After put an empty bar, the same length and resting in every staff, next to it. Before the first bar, the new bar takes over the key, time signature, clefs and tempo, so the piece still opens the same way. Delete Bar takes the chosen bar out; the last bar of a piece always stays. To delete several bars at once, touch a bar and drag across the others to choose a run of bars. The button then reads Delete 3 Bars (or however many you chose). Tap a single bar again to go back to choosing one. Expand Repeats writes the piece out as it is played. You can also touch and hold a bar for a menu with all of this. See The touch and hold menu.
editor-context-menu: The touch and hold menu. Touch and hold a note, rest or bar in the editor for a menu of what you can do to it. In the editor, touch and hold a note, a rest or a bar (or right-click on a Mac) and a menu appears. It changes with what you pressed on. - A note: sharp, flat, natural or back to the key signature; tie to the next note; dotted; half or twice as long; articulation (staccato, accent, tenuto, marcato, fermata); a dynamic from ppp to fff; and turn it into a rest. A tick shows what the note already has. - A rest: half or twice as long, and remove the rest. - A bar: repeat start and end, a crescendo or diminuendo over the bar, add a bar before or after, copy, cut, paste after and duplicate, and delete the bar. A note or rest menu also has a Bar submenu with the same choices for its bar. If you dragged across several bars in Bars or Medley mode first, the bar choices apply to all of them. The menu does not appear in Draw or Erase mode, where holding is part of drawing and erasing. Everything in it can also be done from the mode strip; the menu is a shortcut.
editor-form-mode: Form mode: endings, jumps and tempo marks. First and second time bars, Segno, Coda, To Coda, D.C., D.S., Fine and tempo marks. Form has first and second time bars, jumps (Segno, Coda, To Coda, D.C., D.S., Fine) and tempo marks.
editor-medley-mode: Medley mode: copy, cut and paste bars. Drag across bars to choose them, then Copy, Cut, Paste, Duplicate or Delete, or Insert from Score. Drag across bars to choose them, then Copy, Cut, Paste, Duplicate or Delete. Insert from Score takes bars from another score in your library, which is how you build a medley.
editor-erase-mode: Erase mode. Touch or drag over notes and rests to erase them; double-tap Apple Pencil to switch to the eraser. Touch or drag over notes and rests. A note becomes a rest; a rest comes off the page. Double-tap Apple Pencil to switch to the eraser and back.
editor-draw-mode: Draw mode. Write over the music with Apple Pencil using pen, marker, pencil and colour tools; the ink stays on the page. Write over the music with Apple Pencil, with pen, marker, pencil and colour tools. The ink stays on the page.
edit-a-pdf-score: Edit a score that came from a PDF. The app first reads a PDF, and the editor works on a copy of what it read. A PDF is first read by the app, and the editor works on a copy of what it read. If the app read a scan wrongly, import a MusicXML file of the piece instead, or see Notes in a PDF look wrongly read.
edit-with-apple-pencil-only: Stop a resting hand changing notes. The setting Edit with Apple Pencil Only stops a resting hand changing notes. Editing works with a finger or a Pencil. A setting, Edit with Apple Pencil Only, stops a resting hand changing notes.
save-a-version: Save a version. In the score editor, History and Save Version keep a snapshot you can return to. In the score editor, tap History. Save Version keeps a snapshot you can go back to. Saving in the editor also records one.
start-a-branch: Start a branch to try an idea. New Branch starts a separate line of edits from now or from any earlier version. New Branch starts a separate line of edits, from now or from any earlier version, so you can try something without touching the main score. Switching branches first saves your unsaved edits.
roll-back-a-version: Roll back to an earlier version. Roll Back to This Version restores an earlier snapshot as a new version, so nothing is lost. Roll Back to This Version restores an earlier snapshot as a new version, so nothing is lost and you can undo the roll back.
merge-branches: Merge a branch. Merge brings another branch into the current one, bar by bar. Merge brings another branch into the current one, bar by bar. A bar changed on only one branch comes across.
resolve-merge-clashes: Resolve merge clashes. A bar changed on both branches clashes, and you choose to keep yours or take theirs. A bar changed on both branches clashes, and you choose to keep yours or take theirs. Bars are matched by number, so a bar added or removed early on one branch can make the rest show as clashes.
connect-github: Connect a score to GitHub. Connect a score to your own GitHub repository and push its version history there. You can connect a score to a GitHub repository of your own and push its whole version history there. The app talks to GitHub using a personal access token that you provide. Connecting your own GitHub repositories and adding tracks from them is included even on the Free plan; version history with GitHub sync is part of Professional. GitHub needs the internet.
github-token-safety: Where your GitHub token is kept. The token is kept in your device's Keychain and sent only to GitHub. If you connect a score to a GitHub repository, the app talks to GitHub using a personal access token you provide. The token is kept in your device's Keychain and is sent only to GitHub. Pushing sends your score's versions to the repository you chose, and nothing else.
export-as-musicxml: Export as MusicXML. MusicXML opens in MuseScore, Finale, Sibelius, Dorico, Notion and most other notation apps. Press and hold a score in the library, choose Share, then Export as MusicXML. It opens in MuseScore, Finale, Sibelius, Dorico, Notion and most other notation apps. For a PDF score it is the music the app read from the page.
export-as-pdf: Export as PDF. A PDF score is passed on as it is; any other score is typeset in the key currently shown. Export as PDF gives you the printed page. A PDF score is passed on as it is; any other score is typeset in the key currently shown. Your annotations are included for the key and zoom you are viewing.
print-a-score: Print a score. Print opens the system print dialog. Print opens the system print dialog. It includes your ink for the key and zoom you are viewing.
share-menu: The Share menu. Press and hold a score in the library and choose Share for Export as MusicXML, Export as PDF and Print. Press and hold a score in the library and choose Share. It has Export as MusicXML, Export as PDF and Print.
share-with-airdrop-or-files: Save to Files, AirDrop, email or message. In the share sheet you can save to Files, AirDrop, email or message the file. In the share sheet you can also Save to Files, AirDrop, email or message the file.
export-a-video: Get a video of a score. A video of the music following along can be taken out of the app. Share, Export and Print can also get a video of the score out of the app: a video of the music following along.
start-a-session: Start a Play Together session. Open your parts, choose Play Together, then Start a Session, and allow each player in. Open your parts, then one person chooses Play Together, then Start a Session. The host is asked to allow each player in. Up to eight devices can join one session. Play Together is part of the Performer and Professional plans and works in Advanced mode.
join-a-session: Join a session. Choose Join a Session and pick the host's device. Everyone else chooses Join a Session and picks the host's device. Each player keeps their own part, key and instrument; devices line up bar by bar.
play-together-permissions: Local Network permission. Allow the Local Network permission if asked; devices find each other over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, with no account. Allow the Local Network permission if asked. Devices find each other over Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, with no account. Messages go directly between the devices and are encrypted.
nudge-wireless-audio: Nudge for wireless speakers and headphones. The Nudge slider moves your sound earlier or later if you use wireless speakers or headphones. The Nudge slider moves your sound earlier or later if you use wireless speakers or headphones, so you can line up with the others.
play-together-in-lessons: Using Play Together in lessons and rehearsals. Play, pause, seek and tempo changes on any device are mirrored on all of them. Play, pause, seek and tempo changes on any device are mirrored on all of them, so a teacher and students, or a whole ensemble, stay in step. Each player keeps their own part, key and instrument.
see-the-shortcuts: See the keyboard shortcuts. On a Mac shortcuts are shown in the Playback, Score and View menus; on an iPad hold the Command key. On a Mac nearly everything has a keyboard shortcut, shown in the Playback, Score and View menus. On an iPad with a keyboard, hold the Command key to see them. Single keys (like the space bar) only work when you are not typing in a box.
change-a-shortcut: Change a shortcut. In Settings under Keyboard Shortcuts, click a shortcut and press the keys you want instead. Open Settings ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts. Click a shortcut, then press the keys you want to use instead. Delete takes the shortcut away, and Escape leaves it as it was. A shortcut that is already in use moves to the action you give it to, and the page says so.
reset-shortcuts: Put shortcuts back. The arrow beside a shortcut resets it, and Reset All to Defaults resets them all. The arrow next to a shortcut puts it back, and Reset All to Defaults puts them all back.
open-the-guide-and-support: Open the guide and support from the app. Settings has Guide and Support buttons that open this website inside the app. Settings has two buttons for help: Guide opens this guide and Support opens the support page. Both open inside the app, so you do not leave it. On a Mac, the Help menu and the Add menu on the home screen still open the short built-in help.
appearance-light-dark: Light, dark or system appearance. Appearance is light, dark, or follows the system. Appearance is light, dark or follow the system. Dark sheet music has a default in Settings which any score can override.
highlight-colour: Highlight colour. Highlight Colour chooses the colour that lights up playing notes; the toolbar uses your accent colour. Highlight Colour chooses the colour that lights up playing notes. The toolbar uses your accent colour.
customise-every-colour: Customise every colour. Advanced mode has Customise Every Colour. Advanced mode has Customise Every Colour, for choosing the colours used across the app.
score-defaults: Defaults that any score can override. Zoom, dark sheet music, follow playback and the three highlights have defaults in Settings. Settings has the choices that apply everywhere. Zoom, dark sheet music, follow playback and the three highlights have defaults there, which any score can override.
provide-feedback: Provide feedback from the app. Provide Feedback in Settings posts your title and description to the public feedback board. Provide Feedback in Settings posts what you type, the title and description, to the public feedback board, tagged for Maestro Pro. You can also use the feedback page on the website. Anything you send can be read by anyone, so leave out personal details.
pdf-plays-wrong-number-of-beats: A PDF plays the wrong number of beats. Set Crotchet Beats per Bar in the Inspector, or answer the metre question the first time the score opens. Set Crotchet Beats per Bar in the Inspector, or answer the metre question the first time the score opens.
microphone-cannot-hear-me: Wait for Me or the tuner cannot hear me. Allow the microphone in Settings, raise Microphone Sensitivity, play one note at a time and keep other sound down. 1. Allow the microphone in the device's Settings ▸ Privacy ▸ Microphone. 2. Raise Microphone Sensitivity in Settings ▸ Listening. 3. Play one note at a time and keep other sound down. 4. If it still hears the wrong octave, try Accept Any Octave.
wrong-octave-detected: It hears the wrong octave. Try Accept Any Octave if the tuner or Wait for Me still hears the wrong octave. If it still hears the wrong octave after you have raised the microphone sensitivity, try Accept Any Octave. See also The microphone cannot hear me.
pdf-notes-read-wrongly: Notes in a PDF look wrongly read. Only printed notation can be read and scans need to be straight and clear; try a MusicXML file instead. Only printed notation can be read, and scans need to be straight and clear. For a scan the app cannot read well, import a MusicXML file instead; many are free online.
backing-track-starts-late-or-early: A backing track starts late or early. Drag the track marker, or use Delay Start, then use Match Key and Tempo to Track to listen again. Drag the track marker, or use Delay Start. Use Match Key & Tempo to Track to listen again. For a track with an introduction, set Lead-in Bars.
band-in-a-box-files: Band-in-a-Box files will not open. They cannot be read; save as MusicXML for the notation and as audio for the backing. Band-in-a-Box files cannot be read (a closed format). In Band-in-a-Box, save as MusicXML for the notation and as audio for the backing.
import-does-nothing-or-greyed-out: Import does nothing or a file is greyed out. Choose All Files in the Files browser, or drag the file onto the window. If Import Score does nothing or shows a file greyed out, choose All Files in the Files browser, or drag the file onto the window. Check the file type is one of the supported file types.
jazz-tunes-need-internet: Jazz tunes need the internet. Jazz tunes need an internet connection the first time you add them. Jazz tunes need the internet the first time you add them.
overfull-bar-in-editor: An overfull bar in the editor. Turn Free Editing off, or delete a note and the editor will tidy the bar. Turn Free Editing off, or delete a note and the editor will tidy the bar.
devices-and-compatibility: Devices and compatibility. Which iPhones, iPads and Macs run Maestro Pro, and what is optional. Maestro Pro runs on iPhone, iPad or Mac. iPhone Duo is supported too. Any iPhone or iPad that can run iOS or iPadOS 17 can run Maestro Pro, and newer devices turn pages, engrave and edit a long score more smoothly. Device lists follow Apple's own for iOS 17, iPadOS 17 and macOS 14.
iphone-requirements: iPhone requirements. iOS 17 or later, which covers iPhone XS and later, including iPhone XR and iPhone SE (2nd generation) and later. Maestro Pro needs iOS 17 or later. That covers iPhone XS and later, including iPhone XR and iPhone SE (2nd generation) and later. The layout adapts to the screen: one column on a phone held upright, and more room when it is turned on its side.
iphone-duo: iPhone Duo. On iPhone Duo the music and controls use both screens, and the playback bar folds away for lyrics. iPhone Duo is supported. The music and the controls use the space across both screens, and the playback bar folds away to give lyrics and karaoke the full screen.
ipad-requirements: iPad requirements. iPadOS 17 or later, covering iPad Pro, iPad Air, iPad and iPad mini generations listed here. Maestro Pro needs iPadOS 17 or later. That covers: - iPad Pro: 12.9-inch (2nd generation) and later, 11-inch (all), 10.5-inch - iPad Air: 3rd generation and later - iPad: 6th generation and later - iPad mini: 5th generation and later
mac-requirements: Mac requirements. macOS 14 Sonoma or later, with keyboard shortcuts, multiple windows and trackpad or mouse drawing. Maestro Pro needs macOS 14 Sonoma or later. On a Mac you get the keyboard shortcuts, multiple windows and trackpad or mouse drawing.
apple-pencil: Apple Pencil. Optional: any Apple Pencil that works with your iPad will do, and you do not need one to read, play, transpose or edit. Apple Pencil is optional. You do not need a Pencil to read, play, transpose or edit. Any Apple Pencil that works with your iPad will do: Apple Pencil (1st generation), (2nd generation), (USB-C) or Pro. Which one your iPad takes is listed on Apple's Pencil compatibility page. Annotating on iPad uses Apple Pencil, so your finger still scrolls and taps.
optional-extras: Optional extras the app can use. Microphone, Apple Music, iCloud Drive, local network and the internet are all optional. - Microphone for the tuner, Wait for Me and recording. - Apple Music subscription to play along with a song and see its lyrics. - iCloud Drive to keep your library on all your devices. - Local network permission for Play Together. - Internet to search for scores, lyrics and singers, and for GitHub.
privacy-and-permissions: Privacy and permissions. What stays on your device, what permissions the app asks for, and what is ever sent anywhere. Maestro Pro has no accounts and no adverts, and it does not collect personal data. It does count which features are used, anonymously. Caffeine Media does not receive your scores, recordings or anything else you do in the app. The full policy is on the privacy page.
what-stays-on-your-device: What stays on your device. Your library is stored in the app's folder on your device, or in your own iCloud if you turn it on. Your library (scores, backing tracks, lyrics, drawings, recordings and version history) is stored in the app's folder on your device. If you turn on iCloud Drive, it is kept in the app's iCloud folder in your own iCloud account. That storage belongs to you and Apple; the developer cannot see it.
microphone-permission: Microphone permission. The microphone hears whether you are playing the right note, tunes, and records you, all on the device. The microphone is used to hear whether you are playing the right note, to tune, and to record you. Audio is processed on the device. Recordings are saved only in your library. If the app cannot hear you, allow the microphone in the device's Settings ▸ Privacy ▸ Microphone.
apple-music-permission: Apple Music permission. Apple Music is used to play a song alongside a score and show its lyrics, under your own account. Apple Music is used to play a song from your subscription alongside a score and show its lyrics. This uses Apple's own service under your account.
local-network-permission: Local network permission. Needed so devices can find each other for Play Together; messages go directly between them and are encrypted. The local network permission lets devices find each other for Play Together. Messages go directly between the devices and are encrypted.
when-the-app-uses-the-internet: When the app uses the internet. Only when you ask it to: searching for scores, lyrics or singers, downloading a score, and GitHub. The app uses the internet only when you ask it to. Searching for scores, lyrics or singers sends your search words (and, to match singers, the song title and artist) to the services that answer: the web search engine used for Search Scores and the sites it finds, GitHub, LRCLIB (lyrics) and Genius (singers). Downloading a free score fetches it from the site that hosts it. Those services have their own privacy policies.
usage-statistics: Anonymous usage statistics. Maestro Pro counts which features are used with Aptabase, with no account, name, email or fixed device identifier. Maestro Pro uses Aptabase, a privacy-friendly analytics service hosted in the EU, to count how the app is used. Each event is a short name, such as "play" or "export_pdf", with a few simple details such as a file type or an on/off choice. There is no account, no name, no email address, no advertising identifier and no fixed device identifier, so events cannot be tied back to you. Nothing from your library is ever sent: no score or song titles, lyrics, search words, file names, recordings or drawings.
privacy-feedback-board: Feedback is public. Feedback you send is posted to a public board, so leave out personal details. Provide Feedback in Settings posts what you type, the title and description, to the public feedback board at thecaffeinemediacompany.fider.io, tagged for Maestro Pro. Anything you send there can be read by anyone, so please leave out personal details. Nothing else is sent with it.
getting-started: Getting Started. Maestro Pro is a working tool for musicians: it reads your scores and follows them to the note, turns pages hands-free, rehearses with a backing track, a song from Apple Music, the built-in instrument or a metronome, and lets you write and revise the music itself. The first minute Tap Import Score on the home screen (or the + button, then Import Score) and choose a PDF, MusicXML file or any other supported file. It appears in your library on the left; tap it to open it. Press the big Play button at the bottom. The music plays and follows along. Tap anywhere on the music to start from there, or drag the progress bar. Nothing yet to play? Choose Open Sample on the home screen, or Search Scores to download classical pieces and jazz tunes, or to search the web.
your-library: Your Library. Everything you import lives in the library and stays on the device. It is also kept in iCloud when iCloud Drive is on. Bringing music in Import Score takes PDF, MusicXML (.musicxml, .xml, .mxl), MIDI and karaoke (.mid, .kar), lyrics (.lrc, .txt), CD+Graphics karaoke (.cdg) and Maestro Pro (.maestropro) files. Several can be chosen at once. You can also drag files from the Files app straight onto the window, or choose Maestro Pro from the share sheet of another app (Files, Mail, Safari, Messages…) to import what you are looking at. Import Folder reads every supported file in a folder. In Settings, Link a Folder keeps a folder in step with the library so new files appear by themselves. New Blank Score starts an empty score to write yourself: you choose the name, time signature, key, number of bars, staves (treble, bass or piano) and tempo. Lyrics with Backing: choose a backing track and the app finds its timed lyrics online, for a karaoke-style screen. You can also choose a lyrics file along with the backing track.
playing-a-score: Playing a Score. The bar at the bottom controls playback; the toolbar and the Inspector change how it looks and sounds. Playback controls Play and Pause, skip back and forward by bar, and a progress bar you can drag. The counter shows the bar, beat and time. Tap the music to jump there. On a Mac, Space plays and pauses, the arrow keys skip bars, Return goes to the start and K turns the metronome on or off. Practice Speed slows a piece down or speeds it up without changing the pitch. Type any percentage from 10 to 400 in the box, or use the slider (50 to 150). The tempo is the score's own (from its printed metronome mark) unless you set one: typing a BPM, tapping it or matching a backing track makes it your own, and the Custom Tempo switch under the tempo goes back to the score's. Tap Tempo: tap the tempo (the note and number beside the metronome) and a pad opens with a big Tap key. Tap it in time with the beat; the tempo appears from the second tap and updates with every tap, and a few more make it steadier. It is set as you tap. With a keyboard, the space bar taps while the key is focused. The same pad is under Tempo in the Inspector. Loop: in the Inspector, Loop plays the bars you choose over and over, to practise a hard passage. On a Mac or with a keyboard, [ slows the practice speed and ] speeds it up. Count In plays a bar of clicks before the music. Lead-in Bars sets how many bars of introduction come before bar 1, so a backing track with an intro lines up. The Metronome clicks on every beat.
tuner-wait-for-me: Tuner & Wait for Me. Maestro Pro can listen through the microphone: to tune your instrument, to train a steady note, and to wait for you to play a score note by note. Sound is analysed on the device and is never recorded or sent anywhere. The tuner Open the Tuner from the home screen, the + menu, Settings ▸ Listening, or the tuning fork in a score's toolbar. Play a note: the display shows its name, how many cents sharp or flat it is (a cent is a hundredth of a semitone), and the frequency. The needle sits in the green zone when you are in tune, and the trace below shows the last eight seconds. If your instrument is set to B♭ or E♭ in the Inspector, the written note is shown too. Play Reference Note sounds the note you are aiming for. A = 440 Hz can be changed (415 to 466) for baroque or orchestral tuning.
record-review: Record & Review. Record yourself playing a score, then review the take with the notes lit: green where you should have been, red where you actually were. It listens through the microphone, so it works with any instrument or your voice. Recording Choose Record (the round record button in the toolbar, or More ▸ Record Myself, or ⌘R on a Mac). After the count-in the score plays and you play along. Press Stop, or pause, when you have finished. While you record the built-in instrument and the metronome are muted, so the microphone hears only you. If the score has a backing track the app asks first, because the microphone would hear it: choose Mute It and Record (it comes back afterwards), or Record Anyway if you use headphones. The recording bar has a Mute It button too. The first time, the app asks to use the microphone. Recordings are kept with the score, so they are copied when you duplicate it. Each one is compressed to well under a megabyte a minute.
scales-arpeggios: Scales & Arpeggios. Practice material made on demand. Making a scale Choose Scales & Arpeggios on the home screen, pick the kind (major, minor, blues, arpeggios and more) and a key. A score is created for it and added to the library, ready to play, transpose and slow down.
annotating: Annotating. Mark up the page like a paper part. Drawing on the page Turn on Annotate in the toolbar and draw with Apple Pencil using the tool palette: pens, markers, pencil, colours and an eraser. Ink is saved with the score and shows while you play. Each zoom size keeps its own drawing so it stays lined up with the music. Export as PDF and Print include your ink for the key and zoom you are viewing.
backing-tracks-sound: Backing Tracks & Sound. A backing track is a recording that plays with the score. The built-in instrument can play the notes on the page too. Several tracks A score can have more than one backing track, for example a rhythm section and a separate guide vocal. Add the first with Add Backing Track, then use Add Another Backing Track in the Inspector or the sound menu. They all play together, in time with the score. Under Backing Tracks & Sound each track has its own switch, to turn it off without removing it, and its own level from -24 to +12 decibels. The first track is the one the score keeps time with, and Match Key & Tempo and the track editor work on it. The other tracks follow its speed and key, but not its edit lanes, and should be recordings that start together with it. Reduce Vocals, on any track, cuts the singer down in a stereo recording by cancelling what is in the middle. It leaves a mono track, can take some middle instruments with it, and can't remove a voice from a mono recording.
lyrics-karaoke: Lyrics & Karaoke. Lyrics scroll in time with the music like in Apple Music, and CD+Graphics karaoke files show their built-in pictures. Lyrics files Add a .lrc file (timed lines) or a .txt file to a score from the Lyrics menu. Karaoke MIDI (.kar) files contain their own words. Show Lyrics Instead of Music swaps the page for the words. Animate Syllables swells each syllable as it is sung, and Show Syllable Progress fills it. Typeface, size, alignment and blur for lines not being sung are in Settings. A lyrics-only item (no notation) has its own screen with a transport bar and an optional backing track. Lyrics in seconds or in bars can be chosen when the file has no timing.
writing-editing-music: Writing & Editing Music. The score editor changes the notes in a MusicXML score. A PDF is first read by the app, and the editor works on a copy of what it read. Open it with Edit Score (the music-note-list button; in Simple mode it appears for scores you created). The nine modes The strip at the bottom of the editor has one mode for each kind of job, so the controls for a job are together. Swipe the strip for the rest. Notes: touch a rest and slide up or down to choose the pitch; lift to put a note there, as long as the length chosen below. Drag a note up or down to move it. Scribble back and forth over a note to rub it out. Select a note, then tap a length to change how long it lasts. Rests: tap a note to turn it into a rest of the chosen length. Tap a rest to select it and change its length, or use the bin to take it off the page (the bar keeps its length). Marks: tap a note, then add a sharp, flat or natural, tie it to the next note, or give it staccato, accent, tenuto, marcato or a fermata. Tap one again to take it off. Dynamics: tap a note (the dynamic goes at that note) or a bar (at its start), then choose ppp to fff. Crescendo and Diminuendo put a hairpin over the bar; Longer and Shorter stretch it over more bars. Bars: repeat signs, adding a bar before or after, and deleting one bar or several (drag across them to choose a run). Expand Repeats writes the piece out as it is played. Touch and hold a note, rest or bar for a menu of what you can do to it. Form: first and second time bars, jumps (Segno, Coda, To Coda, D.C., D.S., Fine) and tempo marks. Medley: drag across bars to choose them, then Copy, Cut, Paste, Duplicate or Delete, or Insert from Score to take bars from another score in your library. Erase: touch or drag over notes and rests. A note becomes a rest; a rest comes off the page. Double-tap Apple Pencil to switch to the eraser and back. Draw: write over the music with Apple Pencil, with pen, marker, pencil and colour tools. The ink stays on the page.
version-history-github: Version History & GitHub. Save versions of a score, try ideas on branches, merge them back, and keep it all on GitHub. Versions and branches In the score editor, tap History. Save Version keeps a snapshot you can go back to. Saving in the editor also records one. New Branch starts a separate line of edits, from now or from any earlier version, so you can try something without touching the main score. Roll Back to This Version restores an earlier snapshot as a new version, so nothing is lost and you can undo the roll back. Switching branches first saves your unsaved edits. Merge brings another branch into the current one, bar by bar. A bar changed on only one branch comes across; a bar changed on both clashes, and you choose to keep yours or take theirs. Bars are matched by number, so a bar added or removed early on one branch can make the rest show as clashes.
share-export-print: Share, Export & Print. Get a score, or a video of it, out of the app. Share menu Press and hold a score in the library and choose Share. It has Export as MusicXML, Export as PDF and Print. MusicXML opens in MuseScore, Finale, Sibelius, Dorico, Notion and most other notation apps. For a PDF score it is the music the app read from the page. PDF is the printed page. A PDF score is passed on as it is; any other score is typeset in the key currently shown. Print opens the system print dialog. In the share sheet you can also Save to Files, AirDrop, email or message the file.
play-together: Play Together. Up to eight devices running Maestro Pro can play in time with each other (Advanced mode). Connecting Open your parts, then one person chooses Play Together, then Start a Session. Everyone else chooses Join a Session and picks that device. The host is asked to allow each player in. Allow the Local Network permission if asked. Play, pause, seek and tempo changes on any device are mirrored on all of them, so a teacher and students, or a whole ensemble, stay in step. Each player keeps their own part, key and instrument; devices line up bar by bar. Up to eight devices can join one session. The Nudge slider moves your sound earlier or later if you use wireless speakers or headphones.
keyboard-shortcuts: Keyboard Shortcuts. On a Mac nearly everything has a keyboard shortcut, shown in the Playback, Score and View menus. On an iPad with a keyboard, hold the Command key to see them. Every shortcut can be changed. Changing a shortcut Open Settings ▸ Keyboard Shortcuts. Click a shortcut, then press the keys you want to use instead. Delete takes the shortcut away, and Escape leaves it as it was. A shortcut that is already in use moves to the action you give it to, and the page says so. The arrow next to a shortcut puts it back, and Reset All to Defaults puts them all back. Single keys (like the space bar) only work when you are not typing in a box.
settings-accessibility: Settings & Accessibility. Settings has the choices that apply everywhere. Look and feel Appearance is light, dark or follow the system. Highlight Colour chooses the colour that lights up playing notes; the toolbar uses your accent colour. Advanced mode has Customise Every Colour. Zoom, dark sheet music, follow playback and the three highlights have defaults here, which any score can override.
troubleshooting: Troubleshooting. If something is not right, check here first. Common questions A PDF plays the wrong number of beats: set Crotchet Beats per Bar in the Inspector, or answer the metre question the first time it opens. Wait for Me or the Tuner says it can't hear me: allow the microphone in the device's Settings ▸ Privacy ▸ Microphone, then raise Microphone Sensitivity in Settings ▸ Listening. Play one note at a time and keep other sound down. If it still hears the wrong octave, try Accept Any Octave. Notes in a PDF look wrongly read: only printed notation can be read, and scans need to be straight and clear. For a scan the app cannot read well, import a MusicXML file instead; many are free online. A backing track starts late or early: drag the track marker, or use Delay Start. Use Match Key & Tempo to Track to listen again. Band-in-a-Box files cannot be read (a closed format). In Band-in-a-Box, save as MusicXML for the notation and as audio for the backing. Import Score does nothing or shows a file greyed out: choose All Files in the Files browser, or drag the file onto the window. Jazz tunes need the internet the first time you add them. An overfull bar in the editor: turn Free Editing off, or delete a note and the editor will tidy the bar.
